recommendations.headline: Call satisfaction is the single biggest lever on sales: satisfied calls convert at 70% vs 10% for neutral (56% of all calls) and 2% for dissatisfied (9%), while price is proactively discussed in only 32% of calls even though price_high is the top objection (607 calls, 17%).
behaviour: Price-driven shopping dominates: price_shopper (714, 20%) and comparing_quotes (431, 12%) are the top behaviour tags, with price_enquiry the top intent (1179, 34%).
Pipeline stalls at follow-up: 56% of calls end in callback (1945) vs only 18% in order (620), and rep_missed shows no_follow_up_fixed in 643 calls (18%).
Stock availability is both the #1 stated need (641 mentions) and #2 objection (556, 16%) with a weak 17% win rate, showing it is poorly resolved on calls.
Dealers generate most volume (1816 calls, 52%) but convert at only 31%, below fabricators (36%, 418 calls) and end_users (40%), indicating segment-specific gaps.
Urgent buyers are a real segment (344 tagged, 508 high-urgency calls) but slow/unclear answers (569 calls) and no-quote-sent (361 calls) risk losing them.
satisfaction: Only 30% of calls are rated satisfied (1033/3500), 56% neutral (1945) and 9% dissatisfied (324) - most interactions are merely adequate, not winning.
Satisfaction directly predicts outcome: win rate falls from 70% (satisfied) to 10% (neutral) to just 2% (dissatisfied).
Price is often left unresolved: 68% of calls show price 'not_discussed' (2367), only 8% result in acceptance (286) and 4% end as 'too_high' (131), suggesting reps avoid or delay firm pricing.
Price_high is the most common objection (607 calls, 17%) yet still converts at 22%, better than stock_availability (17%) or competitor_cheaper (12%), showing price alone isn't the main deal-breaker.

conversion.title: Make every call end satisfied, not just neutral
conversion.evidence: Win rate: satisfied 70% vs neutral 10% vs dissatisfied 2% (win_by_satisfaction)
conversion.action: Train reps on a call checklist (greet, confirm need, give clear answer, confirm next step) and have managers review neutral-rated calls weekly to find quick fixes.

conversion.title: Close the follow-up loop
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed in 643 calls (18%); 56% of calls end as callback (1945) with no firm next step
conversion.action: Mandate every call log a specific next action and date in CRM; manager to audit open callbacks over 48 hours old.

conversion.title: Send quotes faster and clearer
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent in 361 calls (10%), slow_or_unclear_answer in 569 calls (16%), price not discussed in 68% of calls
conversion.action: Use a standard rate-sheet template sent via WhatsApp/email within the same call or within 2 hours; track send time.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order flagged in 244 calls (7%)
conversion.action: Coach reps to explicitly ask for PO/confirmation at the end of every price or product discussion.

conversion.title: Improve stock transparency and offer alternatives
conversion.evidence: stock_availability is top need (641) and #2 objection (556, 17% win); didnt_offer_alternative in 263 calls (8%)
conversion.action: Give reps live multi-branch stock visibility and a standard script to propose an alternate size/brand/grade when the exact item is unavailable.

conversion.title: Build segment-specific scripts, especially for unlabelled callers
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment is 863 calls (25%) with only 15% win rate, lowest of all segments
conversion.action: Train reps to quickly qualify caller type (dealer/fabricator/contractor/etc.) in first minute and route to the matching pitch.

conversion.title: Proactively address credit and transport terms
conversion.evidence: credit_terms objection in 162 calls (15% win), transport_cost in 146 calls but 29% win when addressed; needs_credit tagged in 184 calls
conversion.action: Have reps state transport/loading inclusion and current credit policy upfront rather than waiting for the customer to ask.

top_questions.question: Is the material/size in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock across branches immediately on the call; if unavailable, offer a close alternative size/brand and a firm restock date.

top_questions.question: Can you send me the rate/quotation?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send a written quote in the same call via WhatsApp or email using the standard rate-sheet format, not a vague promise to follow up later.

top_questions.question: Can you reduce the price or match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the comparison, explain value factors (certified quality, transport inclusion, reliable supply) before any negotiation, and escalate per policy if needed.

top_questions.question: Does the rate include transport, loading and GST?
top_questions.answer_tip: State all inclusions/exclusions clearly up front in every quote to avoid later disputes.

top_questions.question: When will the vehicle/delivery arrive?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific date and time window, and proactively update the customer rather than waiting for them to call back.

top_questions.question: Can you offer credit terms or LC period?
top_questions.answer_tip: Clearly explain current credit/LC policy and typical terms; flag larger requests for manager approval rather than leaving it open.

top_questions.question: Can you send the test certificate/MTC with the delivery?
top_questions.answer_tip: Make certificate dispatch a standard step with every order confirmation, not something the customer has to chase.

top_questions.question: Can this be cut to custom sizes?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm cutting capability, lead time and any minimum quantity upfront as a value-added service.

recommendations.headline: Varsha lets 56% of calls (1,527 of 2,746) end as vague 'callback' rather than a fixed next step or order, and since satisfied calls close at 72% versus just 10% for neutral calls, tightening follow-up discipline is the single biggest lever to raise conversion.
behaviour: Price shopping and quote comparison dominate (price_shopper 505, comparing_quotes 305) but price_high objection still wins 21% of the time - stock_availability (453 calls) is a bigger blocker at only 18% win rate.
Bulk and urgent buyers are sizeable segments (bulk_buyer 289, urgent_buyer 280) yet delivery_time objection only converts at 15%, showing speed promises aren't being made convincingly.
Credit-seeking customers (needs_credit 146, credit_terms objection 122) convert worst of all at 12% win rate.
258 calls show repeat-buyer behaviour but only 14 are tagged loyal_to_us - loyalty isn't being reinforced on calls.

Price is formally discussed in only 832 of 2,746 calls (accepted 211 + negotiating 518 + too_high 104), meaning price isn't even raised in 70% of calls - a sign quotes/rates aren't being proactively shared.
satisfaction: Only 28.7% of calls end 'satisfied' (788/2,746) while 56.4% are neutral and 10.2% dissatisfied - satisfaction is the strongest predictor of sales, with win rates of 72% (satisfied) vs 10% (neutral) vs 2% (dissatisfied).
No_quote_sent (300 calls) and not_discussed price (1,913 calls) suggest many customers leave without the information needed to decide, which likely drives the large neutral bucket.

Price_high is a top objection (445 calls, 16% of all calls) but still wins 21% of the time - better handling of value beats discounting, since quality_doubt (193) and credit_terms (122) objections convert worse.

recommendations.headline: Venkatesh closes only 16% of calls (123/754) and lets 418 (55%) drift into vague callbacks - the data shows this is a follow-up and closing-discipline problem (130 calls with no fixed follow-up, 70 where he never asked for the order), not a pricing problem.
behaviour: Price shopping dominates: 209 calls (28%) tagged price_shopper and 126 (17%) comparing_quotes, yet in 454 calls (60%) price_reaction was 'not_discussed' - many customers leave without even hearing a firm number.
Most calls end undecided: callback is the top outcome at 418 (55%) vs order at only 123 (16%) and unclear at 116 (15%).
Bulk (107) and urgent (64) buyers are frequent but need fast, certain answers - stock_availability is the single biggest objection (103 calls, only 13% win) and the top stated need (138 mentions).
Repeat buyers (61) and credit-seekers (38) show relationship potential, but credit_terms objection still only wins 25% of the time (40 calls).
Dealers are 58% of all calls (437) and convert at 30%, while fabricators (28 calls) convert highest at 43% - segment handling is uneven.
satisfaction: Satisfaction swings the result completely: satisfied calls win 65% of the time vs just 9% for neutral and 0% for the 44 dissatisfied calls - moving neutral callers to satisfied is the biggest conversion lever available.
53% of calls (397) are rated only 'neutral' on call satisfaction - the majority of Venkatesh's calls leave customers unmoved rather than impressed.

Price itself is rarely the final blocker once discussed: of calls where price was discussed, 75 accepted and 198 moved to negotiation vs only 27 rejected as too_high - the real gap is in closing, not price level.
price_high is the most common objection (162 calls) yet still wins 27% of the time - better value framing, not more discounting, should lift this further.
